title: stabilize-browser-streaming-auth-surface-with-signed-session-nonce-and-compat-layer
author: Sonia Patel
description:
Motivation: improve robustness of browser streaming when using project/org credentials and cookies while standardizing header semantics for scoped ephemeral tokens and request signing. Previously we had multiple ad-hoc behaviors across the compatibility layer that caused intermittent streaming disconnects, CORS header leaks, and ambiguity between Authorization and project-scoped keys. This PR introduces a signed session nonce header, clarifies header precedence, updates the OpenAI-compat mapping for legacy Authorization patterns, and hardens CORS handling for streaming endpoints.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a new header X-RW-Session-Signature (signed nonce) produced by the control plane during session start and validated by streaming workers to prevent mid-stream credential swaps and replay in browsers. Signature uses the existing request-signing key family; implementation reuses canonicalization code but adds streaming pseudo-headers to the signature payload.
- Introduces a clear precedence rule: if X-Project-Key or X-Org-Key is present it wins over Authorization bearer tokens for project-scoped access; scoped ephemeral tokens (claim: "scoped_session") still take precedence when TTL is present. The new precedence table is documented in the header semantics section.
- OpenAI compatibility: we now accept Authorization: Bearer <project_id>:<key> and map it to internal X-Project-Key so legacy clients work without changing their auth flow. This mapping is recorded in audit logs with a masked key.
- Cookie+Streaming fixes: for browser streaming with cookies we now emit Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-RW-Session-Signature,X-RW-Session-Nonce and set SameSite=None on the signed cookie for cross-site clients. The TS SDK streaming helper was updated to set fetch mode 'cors' and credentials 'include' in the example to demonstrate correct behavior.
- Request-signing normalization: lower-case header names for canonical form and include the :method and :path pseudo-headers for signature stability across proxies. This reduces false-negative signature rejections seen when requests transit edge proxies that reorder header casing.
- Telemetry and metrics: new metric rw.streaming.auth.signature_validation{result=ok|fail} and an alert that fires if signature_fail rate > 0.5% for >10m on any region.
- Tests and CI: adds unit tests for nonce validation, E2E that exercises cookie+streaming in a headless browser environment (flaky test isolated and retried in CI), and OpenAI-compat header mapping tests.

Files changed (high level): control-plane/session/controller.go, runtime/streaming/conn_auth.go, runtime/streaming/nonce_validation.go, api/middleware/auth_headers.go, sdk/ts/streaming-client.ts (example), docs/specs/auth-header-semantics.md, docs/compat/openai-auth.md, infra/monitoring/alerts.yaml, tests/e2e/streaming-cookie.spec.ts, tests/unit/signing_normalization_test.go, pkg/audit/audit_logger.go, pkg/http/cors.go

Compatibility notes: The new X-RW-Session-Signature header is additive and will not break existing clients that do not use browser cookie streaming. The Authorization -> X-Project-Key mapping preserves backward compatibility for legacy clients; however operators should rotate keys that use the legacy Authorization format and migrate to explicit X-Project-Key or scoped ephemeral tokens for improved isolation.

Rollout plan: feature gate the signed-nonce validation on runtime nodes for the first week in the canary region (us-west-2) with a soft-fail mode (log & metric but allow) and then flip to hard-fail after metrics look clean. The PR includes the soft-fail toggle and a migration guide in docs/specs/auth-header-semantics.md.

Testing notes: Local unit tests + mocked streaming worker validation; CI initially hit a flaky headless-browser streaming test (see CI section below) which was isolated by increasing the socket timeout in the test harness and adding an explicit wait for the initial signature to arrive. After the fix CI passed on rerun.

Followups:
- ENG-4631: add a short-lived rotation endpoint for session signing keys and wire into the control plane UI.
- PM-1102: update SDK quickstarts to prefer scoped ephemeral tokens for browser examples.

Review conversation summary: See review_threads array for full comments. In short: reviewer asked for additional SameSite/secure cookie tests and audit log masking; I added tests and ensured keys are masked in logs. Reviewer requested to move the signature canonicalization helper out of runtime/streaming into pkg/signing for reuse; refactor done. Final approval granted after E2E flakiness fix and a quick perf check which showed <1% extra CPU on the streaming path.

Marta Ruiz (2026-02-13): Can we keep legacy Authorization mapping behind an opt-in flag? Concerned about audit noise. Response: mapping is enabled by default but we mask keys in audit logs and emit metrics; we added a config toggle for enterprises that want to opt out.

release_notes: Stabilize browser streaming authentication: adds X-RW-Session-Signature for signed nonces, clarifies header precedence (X-Project-Key > Authorization unless scoped token present), OpenAI-compat mapping for legacy Authorization tokens, CORS exposure for session headers, and improvements to canonicalization for request signing. Includes soft-fail rollout toggle and metrics/alerts for signature validation.
